1use crate::third_party::hayro_interpret::cmyk_group::CmykGroup;
2use crate::third_party::hayro_interpret::font::Glyph;
3use crate::third_party::hayro_interpret::soft_mask::SoftMask;
4use crate::third_party::hayro_interpret::{BlendMode, ClipPath, Image};
5use crate::third_party::hayro_interpret::{GlyphDrawMode, Paint, PathDrawMode};

8/// A trait for a device that can be used to process PDF drawing instructions.
9pub trait Device<'a> {
10    /// Set the properties for future stroking operations.
11    /// Set a soft mask to be used for future drawing instructions.
12    fn set_soft_mask(&mut self, mask: Option<SoftMask<'a>>);
13    /// Set the blend mode that should be used for rendering operations.
14    fn set_blend_mode(&mut self, blend_mode: BlendMode);
15    /// Draw a path.
16    fn draw_path(&mut self, path: &BezPath, transform: Affine, paint: &Paint<'a>, draw_mode: &PathDrawMode);
17    /// Push a new clip path to the clip stack.
18    fn push_clip_path(&mut self, clip_path: &ClipPath);
19    /// Push a new transparency group to the blend stack.
20    fn push_transparency_group(&mut self, opacity: f32, mask: Option<SoftMask<'a>>, blend_mode: BlendMode);
21    /// Draw a glyph.
22    fn draw_glyph(
23        &mut self,
24        glyph: &Glyph<'a>,
25        transform: Affine,
26        glyph_transform: Affine,
27        paint: &Paint<'a>,
28        // TODO: Move this into outline glyph.
29        draw_mode: &GlyphDrawMode,
30    );
31    /// Draw an image.
32    fn draw_image(&mut self, image: Image<'a, '_>, transform: Affine);
33    /// Pop the last clip path from the clip stack.
34    fn pop_clip_path(&mut self);
35    /// Pop the last transparency group from the blend stack.
36    fn pop_transparency_group(&mut self);
37    /// Draw a rectangle directly, without going through the general path pipeline.
38    fn draw_rect(&mut self, rect: &Rect, transform: Affine, paint: &Paint<'a>, draw_mode: &PathDrawMode) {
39        self.draw_path(&rect.to_path(0.1), transform, paint, draw_mode);
40    }
41    /// Called at the beginning of a marked content sequence (BMC/BDC).
42    ///
43    /// The tag is the marked content tag (e.g. b"P", b"Span"). The mcid is
44    /// the marked content identifier from the properties dict, if present.
45    fn begin_marked_content(&mut self, _tag: &[u8], _mcid: Option<i32>) {}
46    /// PdfCraft patch (25): the `/ActualText` of the marked content sequence that just began
47    /// (ISO 32000-2 §14.9.4), as the text string's raw bytes. Called right after
48    /// `begin_marked_content`; the text replaces everything drawn up to the matching
49    /// `end_marked_content`.
50    fn actual_text(&mut self, _text: &[u8]) {}
51    /// Called at the end of a marked content sequence (EMC).
52    fn end_marked_content(&mut self) {}
53    /// PdfCraft patch (29): the page's annotations are about to be drawn (until
54    /// `end_annotations`), as page content finishes. Devices can use this to treat their
55    /// paints as annotation colours rather than document colours — the reading-colours
56    /// setting replaces document colours only, never the colours a comment was given.
57    fn begin_annotations(&mut self) {}
58    /// PdfCraft patch (29): the page's annotations are done; what follows is page content.
59    fn end_annotations(&mut self) {}
60    /// PdfCraft patch (39): the transparency group just pushed is a knockout group (`/K true`):
61    /// each of its elements composites with the group's initial backdrop, not with the
62    /// elements drawn before it in the group (ISO 32000-2, knockout groups), until the
63    /// matching `pop_transparency_group`.
64    fn set_knockout(&mut self) {}
65    /// PdfCraft patch (39): an element whose shape is `shape` (device space) is about to be
66    /// drawn into a transparency group of its own. In a knockout group (`set_knockout`) the
67    /// element replaces what the group drew under its shape, so a device clears that first;
68    /// the element's layer then composites over the cleared area as usual.
69    fn knockout_shape(&mut self, _shape: &BezPath) {}
70    /// PdfCraft patch (39): whether `knockout_shape` would clear anything now, that is whether
71    /// the innermost transparency group is a knockout group. Lets the interpreter skip work it
72    /// only needs for the clear.
73    fn in_knockout_group(&mut self) -> bool {
74        false
75    }
76    /// PdfCraft patch (39): `image`, an unmasked raster image, is about to be drawn with
77    /// `transform` in a knockout group. A device that will draw it (it isn't skipped and it
78    /// decodes) clears what the group drew under its placement rectangle first, so the image
79    /// replaces it. Decided by the device, at the size it draws the image, so the draw reuses
80    /// that decode.
81    fn knockout_image(&mut self, _image: &crate::third_party::hayro_interpret::RasterImage<'_>, _transform: Affine) {}
82    /// PdfCraft patch (39): whether a transparency group drawn now is an element of a knockout
83    /// group that the device wants cleared under the group's shape first. If so the
84    /// interpreter draws the group's content once between `begin_knockout_erase` and
85    /// `end_knockout_erase`, in which every paint clears what is under its shape instead of
86    /// painting, and then draws the group as usual, in a layer of its own.
87    fn knockout_erase_wanted(&mut self) -> bool {
88        false
89    }
90    /// PdfCraft patch (39): see `knockout_erase_wanted`.
91    fn begin_knockout_erase(&mut self) {}
92    /// PdfCraft patch (39): see `knockout_erase_wanted`.
93    fn end_knockout_erase(&mut self) {}
94    /// PdfCraft patch (67): the knockout group just pushed (`set_knockout`) is drawn once per
95    /// blend mode its elements use, each pass into a layer of its own composited with that
96    /// mode. In this pass only elements whose blend mode is `mode` paint; every other element
97    /// clears what is under its shape, as it would replace it. Each pixel then holds the last
98    /// element covering it in exactly one pass, which composites it with the group's backdrop
99    /// in that element's own blend mode (#4886).
100    fn begin_knockout_pass(&mut self, _mode: BlendMode) {}
101    /// PdfCraft patch (67): ends the pass `begin_knockout_pass` started, before the layer is
102    /// popped. Returns the other blend modes the pass's elements used, each once. A device
103    /// that doesn't track them returns none, and the group is drawn in one Normal pass.
104    fn end_knockout_pass(&mut self) -> Vec<BlendMode> {
105        Vec::new()
106    }
107    /// PdfCraft patch (70): draw the contents of an isolated transparency group that blends
108    /// in `DeviceCMYK` (ISO 32000-2 §11.3.4), already inside the layer it is composited
109    /// through. Return `true` when the device drew them; on `false` (the default) the
110    /// interpreter draws the contents into the device as for any other group.
111    fn draw_isolated_cmyk_group(&mut self, _group: &CmykGroup<'a, '_>) -> bool {
112        false
113    }
114    /// PdfCraft patch (70): an isolated transparency group that names a blending colour space
115    /// other than `DeviceCMYK` is about to be drawn. A device drawing an enclosing group in CMYK
116    /// can no longer draw that group right, since this one blends in its own space.
117    fn group_blends_outside_device_cmyk(&mut self) {}
118}

120/// A device that discards all drawing operations.
121pub struct DummyDevice;
122
123impl Device<'_> for DummyDevice {
124    fn set_soft_mask(&mut self, _: Option<SoftMask<'_>>) {}
125    fn set_blend_mode(&mut self, _: BlendMode) {}
126    fn draw_path(&mut self, _: &BezPath, _: Affine, _: &Paint<'_>, _: &PathDrawMode) {}
127    fn push_clip_path(&mut self, _: &ClipPath) {}
128    fn push_transparency_group(&mut self, _: f32, _: Option<SoftMask<'_>>, _: BlendMode) {}
129    fn draw_glyph(&mut self, _: &Glyph<'_>, _: Affine, _: Affine, _: &Paint<'_>, _: &GlyphDrawMode) {}
130    fn draw_image(&mut self, _: Image<'_, '_>, _: Affine) {}
131    fn pop_clip_path(&mut self) {}
132    fn pop_transparency_group(&mut self) {}
133}
